metadata.title: How teachers’ enthusiasm influences Chinese students’ school belonging: The mediation role of teaching practices

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata for Chinese students from four participating cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Jiangsu) and analyzes students nested within schools using multilevel mediation models. The manuscript describes PISA’s stratified two-stage sampling (schools sampled first, then students within schools) and motivates multilevel modeling to capture within-school homogeneity and between-school variation, but it does not report whether PISA sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in estimation. No PISA weight variable name (e.g., student/sampling weights) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is mentioned, so weight usage cannot be confirmed from the text. Because the analysis is based on multilevel linear mediation (not ML algorithms), the paper should ideally clarify whether complex survey weights were used to produce population-representative estimates for the Chinese PISA target population.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables (school belonging and the four teacher-related scales) are scaled using IRT weighted likelihood estimates (WLE), but the manuscript does not describe any missing-data handling procedure for item nonresponse or missing questionnaire responses. This is a reporting gap because PISA datasets typically contain nontrivial missingness across items and background measures, and mediation estimates can be sensitive to how missingness is treated. The paper therefore provides insufficient transparency to assess potential bias from missing responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analytic sample is restricted to Chinese students participating in PISA 2018 from four cities: Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu. The study includes 361 Chinese schools initially, then drops one school with only one student, yielding 360 schools. The final sample contains 12,057 students (with an average of 34.01 students per school). No additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., missing-item thresholds, complete-case criteria) are reported in the provided text.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (China; four cities) — school belonging (SCHBLNG) scale (WLE)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel mediation Model 0 (total effect): est.=0.272, se.=0.010, p<.01; SD of random effects (teacher enthusiasm slope across schools)=0.102. Model 2 (direct/unmediated effect): est.=0.179, se.=0.012, p<.01.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (China; four cities) the study leveraged Teacher enthusiasm to predict School belonging (SCHBLNG; WLE score), finding that teacher enthusiasm had a positive total effect (est.=0.272) and a smaller but still significant direct effect after accounting for teaching practices (est.=0.179). This indicates that strengthening teacher enthusiasm may be a practical lever for improving students’ sense of belonging, though the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (China; four cities) — school belonging (SCHBLNG) scale (WLE)
main_findings.target_variable: School belonging (SCHBLNG; WLE score) — mediator effects (Model 2)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Model 2 mediator paths to SCHBLNG: Teacher support est.=0.061, se.=0.012, p<.01; Perceived teacher feedback est.=0.062, se.=0.012, p<.01; Teacher-directed instruction est.=0.044, se.=0.011, p<.01; Adaptivity of instruction est.=0.023, se.=0.011, p>.05.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (China; four cities) the study leveraged Teacher support, Perceived teacher feedback, Teacher-directed instruction, and Adaptivity of instruction to predict School belonging (SCHBLNG; WLE score), finding that teacher support and feedback were significant while adaptivity was not significant in the direct mediator model. This indicates that policies and professional development should prioritize supportive and feedback-oriented teaching behaviors to foster belonging, rather than focusing only on instructional adaptivity.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (China; four cities) — school belonging (SCHBLNG) scale (WLE)
main_findings.target_variable: Mediation effects of teaching practices between teacher enthusiasm and school belonging
main_findings.performance_metrics: Average mediation effects across schools: total mediated share=33.14% of total effect; Teacher feedback is the most important mediator. Average mediation effect sizes: Teacher support=0.024 (8.97%); Perceived teacher feedback=0.033 (12.33%); Teacher-directed instruction=0.017 (6.10%); Adaptivity of instruction=0.016 (5.77%). Monte Carlo 95% CIs for mediation effects are all above 0.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (China; four cities) the study leveraged Teacher support, Perceived teacher feedback, Teacher-directed instruction, and Adaptivity of instruction to estimate mediation between Teacher enthusiasm and School belonging (SCHBLNG; WLE score), finding that teaching practices jointly mediated 33.14% of the total effect and that teacher feedback was the largest mediator (average mediation effect=0.033). This indicates that improving how enthusiastic teachers provide feedback and support may be an effective pathway for translating teacher enthusiasm into stronger student belonging, while causality cannot be established due to the cross-sectional mediation framework.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2018 microdata for Chinese students from four participating cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; N=12,057 students across 360 schools) to examine how teacher enthusiasm relates to students’ school belonging and whether four teaching practices mediate this relationship. School belonging (SCHBLNG) and the teacher-related scales are IRT-scaled using weighted likelihood estimates (WLE), with OECD-referenced scaling (mean 0, SD 1). The analysis applies multilevel mediation models (1–1–1) to account for students nested within schools and reports that teacher enthusiasm has a significant positive total effect on school belonging (est.=0.272, se.=0.010, p<.01) and a smaller direct effect after mediators (est.=0.179, se.=0.012, p<.01). Teaching practices jointly mediate 33.14% of the total effect, with teacher feedback the largest mediator (average mediation effect=0.033). Limitations include lack of reported missing-data handling and the cross-sectional design, which constrains causal claims about the mediation pathways.
